newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Atlantic Treaty Association backs Bulgaria NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Treaty Association backs Bulgaria NATO bid.

text.p: The Secretary-General of the Atlantic Treaty Association (ATA) said on Tuesday that he backed Bulgaria's early admission in NATO in a bid to help promote stability in the turbulent Balkan region.
"It is more than desirable that Bulgaria join the alliance with the first wave of new members," Alfred Cahen told reporters after meeting President Petar Stoyanov.
Cahen, who arrived on Monday on a two-day visit to Sofia, said he was a strong advocate of Bulgaria's early membership of NATO.
"First of all, Bulgaria has a lot to give to the alliance, namely it can help promote stability in a very sensitive region of the Balkans," Cahen said.
The ATA, founded in 1954, aims to inform public opinion on NATO.

Comprised of non-governmental committees in member states, it serves as an important forum for dialogue with pro-NATO organisations in countries which have Partnership for Peace agreements with the alliance.
Cahen said that if Bulgaria would not be among the first group of countries admitted to the alliance, it should be among the second group.
The ATA's 43rd assembly will take place in Sofia in October. It will be the first time the assembly will meet in a country which is not a NATO member.
Bulgaria's new reformist government, in office since May 21, says it wants to join NATO.
NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana is expected to prepare a shortlist of candidates ahead of a July Madrid summit.
Several NATO states have expressed support for inviting as many as five new members into the alliance. Former Warsaw Pact members Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the favourites.
